instruction.text: What do you think brought the plague to an end?

feedback.end: A very cold winter killed most rats carrying the plague. This meant that the disease stopped spreading and slowly disappeared in England. The Great Fire of London likely helped stop the plague too!

instruction.text: Much of what we know about the Great Plague come from Bills of Mortality. Select the number of plague deaths to learn more.

feedback.finish: Bills of Mortality were weekly records of deaths and their causes in London. Information on plague victims were collected by plague doctors and people called searchers.

instruction.text: We also get a lot of information from the diary of Samuel Pepys. Select it to learn more.
instruction.sound: We also get a lot of information from the diary of Samuel Peeps. Select it to learn more.

atoms.b: Samuel Pepys lived in ((++London Germany)) during the Great Plague.
His diaries are very ((++helpful useless)) to historians for knowing about important events, such as ((++the_Great_Plague the_weather)) and the Great Fire of London.
In his diaries, he wrote about the ((++spread jam)) of the plague and how people were ((++reacting dancing)) to it.

instruction.text: Listen to what Samuel Pepys wrote and choose the correct statement.
instruction.sound: Listen to what Samuel peeps wrote and choose the correct statement.

atoms.a: “Today, I saw two or three houses marked with a red cross upon the doors... It made me nervous.”

b.sound: Samuel Pepys was scared of the plague.

atoms.a: “There are great fears of the sickness here in the city... two or three houses are already shut up.”

b.sound: People got locked in their houses to stop the plague from spreading.
Ill people were allowed to go to parties.
The plague didn’t spread at all.
